question: Assume today is 2026-10-27. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of UK residential property transactions (with a value of £40,000 or above) in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as it will be first reported (provisional estimate) in HM Revenue & Customs' monthly release 'Monthly property transactions completed in the UK with value of £40,000 or above'.

target.what: Number of UK residential property transactions with value £40,000 or above completed in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first provisionally reported by HMRC in its monthly 'Monthly property transactions completed in the UK with value of £40,000 or above' release
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to cutoff (2026-10-27) but the provisional HMRC figure for September 2026 would typically be published in late October 2026, so it may or may not yet be public at cutoff; treat as a first-provisional estimate. candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 SA transaction count will be close to the recent trend of HMRC monthly SA residential transactions (e.g. 2024-2026 monthly values), adjusted for September seasonality and any recent momentum. The most recent published months before cutoff (e.g. July/August 2026) anchor the level.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC monthly UK residential property transactions >= £40k, seasonally adjusted, monthly values for 2023-01 through the latest month published before 2026-10-27 (ideally July or August 2026). Also the same month (September) in 2023, 2024, 2025 to gauge September seasonal level. Minimum: last 12 monthly SA values.

candidates.perspective: Land Registry / ONS house price and sales volumes
candidates.hypothesis: HM Land Registry Price Paid Data / ONS UK House Price Index sales volumes for England & Wales (and equivalent Registers of Scotland, NI) provide an independent transaction count that can be scaled to UK total and compared to HMRC. If HMLR volumes for recent months are available, they constrain the HMRC level via a stable coverage ratio.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
